claim: Virus-like particle (VLP) is a kind of multiprotein structure organized as virus that can deliver therapeutic substances into cells and stimulate immune response.
source: Virus-like particle (VLP), which is a kind of multiprotein structure organized as virus, can deliver therapeutic substances into cells and stimulate immune response.

source: However, the weak targeted delivery of VLP in vivo and its susceptibility to neutralization by antibodies hinder their clinical applications.

claim: A novel protein carrier was designed using the mammalian-derived capsid protein PEG10, which can self-assemble into endogenous VLP (eVLP) with high protein loading and transfection efficiency.
source: Here, we first designed a novel protein carrier using the mammalian-derived capsid protein PEG10, which can self-assemble into endogenous VLP (eVLP) with high protein loading and transfection efficiency.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: An engineered tumor vaccine, named ePAC, was developed by packaging genetically encoded neoantigen into eVLP with further modification of CpG-ODN on its surface.
source: Then, an engineered tumor vaccine, named ePAC, was developed by packaging genetically encoded neoantigen into eVLP with further modification of CpG-ODN on its surface to serve as an adjuvant and targeting unit to dendritic cells (DCs).

claim: CpG-ODN on the surface of ePAC serves as an adjuvant and targeting unit to dendritic cells (DCs).

claim: ePAC can efficiently target and transport neoantigens to DCs.

claim: ePAC promotes DCs maturation to induce neoantigen-specific T cells.

claim: Lentiviruses offer an excellent approach to cross cell membranes by interacting with specific host cell receptors through viral envelope glycoproteins.
source: Lentiviruses offer an excellent approach to cross cell membranes by interacting with specific host cell receptors through viral envelope glycoproteins (Sundquist and Kräusslich, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Sundquist and Kräusslich, 2012.

claim: The protein of interest (POI) is always directly fused to lentiviral structural proteins for transduction to ensure safe gene delivery without permanent integration into the human genome.
source: To ensure safe gene delivery without permanent integration into the human genome, the protein of interest (POI) is always directly fused to lentiviral structural proteins for transduction (Voelkel et al., 2010; Kaczmarczyk et al., 2011; Cai et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: The POI can be inserted into the C-terminal of matrix protein (MA), core capsid (CA), nucleocapsid (NC), or even integrase (IN) with a protease site.
source: Specifically, the POI can be inserted into the C-terminal of matrix protein (MA), core capsid (CA), nucleocapsid (NC), or even integrase (IN) with a protease site, allowing for independent functions upon cleavage by viral protease (Voelkel et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Voelkel et al., 2010.

claim: In the delivery of CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoproteins, the lentiviral gag domain, including MA and NC, were fused with Cas9 and mixed with the full-length gag-pol domain for virus-like particle (VLP) packaging.
source: For example, in the delivery of CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoproteins, the lentiviral gag domain, including MA and NC, were fused with Cas9 and mixed with the full-length gag-pol domain for virus-like particle (VLP) packaging; upon transfection, Cas9 was cleaved by the protease from the viral pol domain in the host cell, leading to excellent gene editing efficiency (Mangeot et al., 2019; Hamilton et al., 2021; An et al., 2024; Hamilton et al., 2024).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Upon transfection, Cas9 was cleaved by the protease from the viral pol domain in the host cell, leading to excellent gene editing efficiency.
source: For example, in the delivery of CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoproteins, the lentiviral gag domain, including MA and NC, were fused with Cas9 and mixed with the full-length gag-pol domain for virus-like particle (VLP) packaging; upon transfection, Cas9 was cleaved by the protease from the viral pol domain in the host cell, leading to excellent gene editing efficiency (Mangeot et al., 2019; Hamilton et al., 2021; An et al., 2024; Hamilton et al., 2024).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to multiple studies.
